summary: This standards-track RFC defines how to advertise one or more S-BFD Discriminators using the IS-IS Router CAPABILITY TLV.

plainLanguage.summary: S-BFD nodes need to learn the discriminator values that other nodes have reserved. This RFC defines an optional IS-IS sub-TLV that carries those values and can be flooded within an area or across a domain.

questions: how does is-is flood s-bfd discriminators
how does is-is advertise s-bfd discriminators
subtitle: An IS-IS Router CAPABILITY sub-TLV advertises S-BFD discriminator values.

tldr.problem: Seamless Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (S-BFD) requires nodes to know discriminators reserved by other nodes.
tldr.mechanism: A new sub-TLV, type 20, carries one or more four-octet discriminators inside an IS-IS Router CAPABILITY TLV.
tldr.outcome: An IS may flood the values within an area or throughout the domain, depending on intended S-BFD use.

today: RFC 7883 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Discriminators Are Advertised
sections.content:
RFC 7880 defines a simplified mechanism for Bidirectional Forwarding Detection called Seamless BFD (S-BFD). It depends on network nodes knowing the discriminator values that each node reserves.

This RFC defines one way to advertise those values: use the Intermediate System to Intermediate System (IS-IS) routing protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: S-BFD needs each node to know discriminator values reserved by other nodes. IS-IS can distribute those values through the network.

sections.title: The Discriminator Sub-TLV
sections.content:
The IS-IS Router CAPABILITY TLV carries a new S-BFD Discriminators sub-TLV. Its type is 20 and takes one octet, its length takes one octet and must be a multiple of four, and its payload contains four octets per discriminator.

The sub-TLV is optional, and an IS MAY advertise several. The mapping of a discriminator to a particular use is outside this RFC's scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The optional field lists discriminator values, with four octets for each one. This RFC does not define what each value is used for.

sections.title: Flooding Scope
sections.content:
Advertisements MAY be flooded within an IS-IS area or throughout the domain, using RFC 4971 procedures. The intended S-BFD use determines the scope.

Area scope is appropriate when use stays within a Level-1 area. Domain scope is appropriate when use spans different Level-1 areas.
sections.plainLanguage: Choose where the advertisement travels based on where S-BFD will be used. A local use can stay within an area; a use across areas can be flooded through the domain.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
IANA registered value 20, named S-BFD Discriminators, in the Sub-TLVs for TLV 242 registry. The new sub-TLV adds no new security risks for IS-IS.

Advertising discriminators can let attackers initiate S-BFD sessions using the advertised information. RFC 7880 discusses those vulnerabilities and mitigations.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA added the new sub-TLV number to its registry. Publishing discriminator values can enable attempts to start S-BFD sessions, a risk discussed in RFC 7880.
